hook: A kelp suppresses asexual development when potential mates are present.
summary: Researchers compared gene expression and development in the kelp Laminaria pallida across sexual and asexual routes, plus two natural populations. Asexual reproduction came with endoreduplication and lower fitness, and it was rarely used in the wild. This suggests asexuality is a backup when mates are scarce; the work covers one species and two populations.
title: Life-cycle plasticity enables conditional asexual reproduction in a kelp.
